findings.title: Coverage map omits 17 acceptance criteria and invents one non-criterion
findings.body: The claimed total of 210 is not the specs' acceptance inventory. The specs contain 206 `Acceptance` bullets plus 20 explicitly counted numbered criteria, for 226 criteria. The map omits FR-A6 bullets 4 and 7; FR-A10 bullet 7; FR-B3 bullet 2; FR-B6 bullets 6–8; FR-C1 bullet 4; FR-M1 bullet 7; FR-M2 bullet 4; FR-M7 bullet 3; FR-D3 bullet 3; FR-D9 bullet 2; FR-S1 bullets 4, 6, and 7; and FR-S8 bullet 2. It also turns Spec B FR-S3's non-acceptance `Consequence (owner terms)` into a third criterion. These omissions leave binding launch, retirement, prose, tripwire, transition, native-channel, consumer-report, and stripped-change requirements without exactly-once ownership.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate the map directly from every `Acceptance` bullet plus the two declared numbered sections, preserve each spec bullet's ordinal, allocate the 17 missing rows, remove the FR-S3 consequence row, and recalculate counts.
findings.evidence: Examples: Spec A FR-A6's launch-word convention and post-reset no-exemption rules are at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:327 and :349 but the map jumps from FR-A6's third acceptance to the later `tiers order entry` text at package/coverage-map.md:36. Spec A FR-B6 has nine acceptance bullets at lines 791–864, while package/coverage-map.md:88–93 carries only six. Spec B FR-S1 has ten acceptance bullets at lines 906–1016, while package/coverage-map.md:198–204 carries seven. The stated 210-row total therefore masks omissions.

findings.title: C17 cannot deliver the machinery-definition criterion allocated to it
findings.body: The map assigns Spec A FR-E1's binding definition and labeling rules for `machinery` to C17, but C17's What promises only the thirteen configuration values, their fail direction, and dependency checks. It never promises to land the machinery definition, classification test, judgment-only rule, issue labels, or calibration-time label creation. Its declared owner therefore cannot deliver the allocated criterion.
findings.suggestion: Add the complete FR-E1 machinery-definition and label outcome to C17's What and DoD, or allocate it to the child that owns the issue-contract routing vocabulary.
findings.evidence: package/coverage-map.md:115 assigns FR-E1 acceptance bullet 2 to C17. The criterion in specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1021–1041 defines machinery, its classification test, who applies it, the two labels, and their creation during calibration. None appears in C17's What or DoD.

findings.title: C4 instructs builders to keep parity sentences that the spec orders removed
findings.body: C4's What says CONVENTIONS keeps the existing parity sentences as the Codex position. The stamped host rule explicitly says those sentences go. C4's own DoD then demands that no parity sentence remain, leaving the issue internally contradictory about the primary edit.
findings.suggestion: Replace the `keeping the existing parity sentences` instruction with the ruled three-part disclosed-absence wording and make What agree with the DoD.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-F4 says, `The parity sentences go ("the same methodology, no behavior changes"; "bare CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fails on Codex")` at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1343–1348. C4 line 3 says to keep them, while C4 line 6 says CONVENTIONS must contain no parity sentence.

findings.title: The glossary contract does not contain every ruled glossary term
findings.body: R1 claims to enumerate every ruled term, but omits a substantial portion of Spec A FR-F9's seed. C1's DoD checks only the incomplete R1 list, so the promised canonical glossary can pass while lacking binding terms such as plugin component, retirement condition and its three shapes, real catch/noise, citation, consumer evidence, unmeasured, fired, proposal, retirement ruling, foundational component, authority surface, priority tiers, dial/N and lane names, child names, kind label, always-loaded set, keep list, rail, doctrine surface, foreign catch, and machinery-map threat tags.
findings.suggestion: Expand R1 to cover the complete FR-F9 seed verbatim in substance, then make C1's DoD compare the glossary against FR-F9 or the corrected complete register entry.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-F9 enumerates the glossary seed at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1466–1561. R1's purported complete list at package/register.md:18 omits many of those entries, while package/children/C1.md:8 grades only `every term in register entry R1`.

findings.title: R5 corrupts the receipt's state/cause and provenance schema
findings.body: R5 mixes `cap` and `cannot-certify` into the cause set, omits the `certified` terminal state and the concrete non-loop causes, and names provenance `driver-observed` instead of the stamped `dispatch-observed`. C12's DoD explicitly requires every R5 field, so following the register would implement a different receipt schema from the spec.
findings.suggestion: Separate terminal state (`certified`, `cap`, `cannot-certify`) from cause (loop reasons plus `budget` and `open findings`) and use the stamped per-seat provenance values `dispatch-observed` and `hand-landed`.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8 defines terminal state and cause separately at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:733–739 and names per-seat provenance `dispatch-observed or hand-landed` at :787–793. R5 instead lists cap/cannot-certify among causes and uses `driver-observed`; C12 consumes that text at package/children/C12.md:18.

findings.title: R7 rejects the hand-landed evidence path the spec requires
findings.body: R7 says absent telemetry always refuses, but the stamped rule has an explicit exception for hand-landed results, which have no telemetry and use FR-D2's execution-evidence binding instead. C12 simultaneously quotes R7 and promises that a hand-landed specimen certifies, creating incompatible implementation instructions.
findings.suggestion: Add the hand-landed exception to R7: absent telemetry refuses for runner-observed seats, while hand-landed seats use the FR-D2 execution-evidence binding.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-M2 states `A seat with no telemetry (a hand-landed result) reads FR-D2's execution-evidence binding instead` at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:231–243. R7 has no exception, while package/children/C12.md:9 requires a hand-landed result to certify.

findings.title: R8 requires an echo from MOVE rows that the spec says must read nothing
findings.body: R8 says the C1 annex's MOVE rows all read tolerantly with a loud echo. The stamped derivation expressly permits a MOVE disposition to drop a demand, in which case it reads nothing, resolves no caller input, emits no echo, and appears in neither envelope half. C10's What repeats the erroneous all-MOVE echo rule even though its DoD later permits dropped rows.
findings.suggestion: Qualify R8 and C10's What so accepted/defaulted MOVE rows echo resolved input, while dropped MOVE rows read and echo nothing.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-M1 defines dropped MOVE rows at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:141–144. R8 applies tolerant reading and echo to every MOVE row; package/children/C10.md:3 repeats that instruction, while line 7 recognizes the dropped alternative.

findings.title: C6 lands plain keeps where the spec requires conditional keeps immediately
findings.body: C6 says the first state of every entry is `plain keep`. The stamped rollout rule says plain keep is only the pre-rollout failure direction; when a component's line lands it immediately becomes `keep-until-condition-fires`. Building the issue as written would land the wrong initial state for the entire list.
findings.suggestion: State that every non-foundational entry lands as `keep-until-condition-fires`; reserve plain keep only for components whose rollout line has not yet landed.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B3 says `keep becomes keep-until-condition-fires the moment its line lands; until then it is a plain keep` at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:712–718. C6's work is precisely to land all lines, yet package/children/C6.md:3 calls their first state plain keep.

findings.title: C16 parks a gotcha family the specs require to retire
findings.body: C16 separates the untrusted-git gotcha family from the retiring hostile-repo defenses and says it is parked and never deleted. Both stamped specs name that gotcha family as part of what retires in the sanitized-view shrink.
findings.suggestion: Include the gotcha family in the element-by-element retirement inventory and remove the `parked, never deleted` outcome unless the owner amends the specs.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-F3 says `The untrusted-tree hardening and the untrusted-git gotcha family retire` at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1323–1326. Spec B FR-S8 repeats that the hardening and gotcha family retire at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1157–1164 and :1184–1188. C16 line 3 and DoD line 9 instead preserve the gotcha family.

findings.title: C7 introduces an ungradable prose-size gate and omits two promised outcomes
findings.body: `One screen` has no defined viewport, rendering, line count, or command, so a vet cannot grade it from the handback. It also recreates the size target the spec explicitly rejects. Separately, C7's DoD never checks the promised check-runner home or the launch-doctrine conformance-probe step.
findings.suggestion: Delete the one-screen gate and grade the charter structurally. Add explicit artifact checks for the check-runner's home and the launch section's conformance-probe pointer.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B6 says there is no target size at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:852–863. C7 What promises the check-runner and launch-doctrine work at package/children/C7.md:3, but DoD lines 6–10 do not mention either.

findings.title: Seven children quote R28 despite not being named as consumers
findings.body: R28 names only C3, C5, C7, and C10–C16 as consumers, but C1, C2, C4, C6, C8, C9, and C17 also quote it. This violates the register's exact consumer/quote contract. C1 and C2 demonstrably touch tests, so the consumer list is also substantively incomplete, not merely over-quotation.
findings.suggestion: Add every quoting child that really touches tests to R28's Consumers line and remove R28 from children that do not touch tests.
findings.evidence: Extra quotations occur at package/children/C1.md:28, C2.md:34, C4.md:32, C6.md:26, C8.md:25, C9.md:21, and C17.md:23. R28's Consumers line at package/register.md:128 excludes all seven.

findings.title: Wave 1 runs children beside C1 despite the mandatory first-seam ordering
findings.body: The sequencing paragraph first says C1 is first, then places C9, C16, C10, C12, and C17 beside it in Wave 1. Those children consume vocabulary and other contracts owned by C1, yet their issue bodies do not say `after C1`. This allows them to build against a seam that has not landed, contrary to the only globally fixed ordering.
findings.suggestion: Make C1 a prerequisite wave of its own, then launch the current Wave 1 children only after C1 lands.
findings.evidence: Spec A fixes `founding-documents first as the shared seam` at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1167–1174. The map calls the other children `Wave 1 beside it`, and, for example, package/children/C10.md:12 says only `Wave 1` while consuming R1.

findings.title: C12's six-case acceptance test is not present in the issue body
findings.body: The DoD says each expected answer must match the six cases `as quoted in this body`, but the child never quotes those six cases. Neither What nor its register entries enumerate them. A vet limited to the PR, its body, and CI therefore cannot tell whether the required suite contains the right cases.
findings.suggestion: Quote the six FR-D8 cases and their expected outcomes in C12, or add a complete register entry for them and consume it here.
findings.evidence: The authoritative cases are enumerated at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:797–814. C12 quotes R1, R5, R6, R7, R23, R24, R26, R27, and R28, none of which contains the six-case list.

findings.title: C10's DoD omits several load-bearing dispatch outcomes
findings.body: C10 promises effort echo and source, self-describing refusals, the one-hour cell-granularity cache, the refusal-streak contract line, and the dispatch-mechanics envelope. None has a pass/fail DoD bullet. The PR can satisfy the listed allowlist, MOVE-row, generated-doc, and ledger checks while omitting these promised outcomes.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit DoD checks for effort/source recording, refusal remedy text, 3600-second cell cache behavior, the FR-S7 streak line, and the complete variance-envelope declaration.
findings.evidence: The omitted outcomes are promised at package/children/C10.md:3 and required by Spec B FR-M3–M5, FR-S3, FR-S6, and FR-S7. DoD lines 6–10 do not test them.

findings.title: C11's DoD does not grade the selftest correction or native-channel operating costs
findings.body: C11 promises that the selftest doc will say it proves configuration rather than liveness and that output/completion adapters and progress signals will be restated for native channels. Its DoD checks neither outcome, so a handback can pass while retaining the misleading selftest claim or broken progress/completion behavior.
findings.suggestion: Add artifact checks for the exact selftest limitation and recorded tests for result production, completion detection, and progress telemetry on every supported mode.
findings.evidence: The promises are in package/children/C11.md:3 and Spec B FR-S5 at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1064–1073. C11 DoD lines 6–10 cover typed results, cursor selection, a broken probe, and journal fields only.

findings.title: C13's DoD omits the fail-closed guidance row and every-terminal receipt call
findings.body: C13 promises that the guidance-channel row stands, the receipt writer runs at certification and every terminal, round-driver refusals name accepted shapes, the echo set is complete, and the round-driver envelope is declared. Its DoD does not grade any of those outcomes. In particular, the owner-protected guidance channel could be weakened while every listed DoD bullet passes.
findings.suggestion: Add pass/fail bullets for the ground-(b) guidance row, receipt generation at each terminal kind, remedy-bearing refusals, the complete echo set, and the declared envelope.
findings.evidence: These outcomes appear in package/children/C13.md:3. Spec B FR-D4 makes any non-KEEP disposition of the guidance row park owner-ward at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:526–541, and FR-D8 requires the writer at every terminal at :711–732.

findings.title: C14 leaves most CLI-Claude safety and conformance promises ungraded
findings.body: C14's DoD verifies typed results, argv retirement, and the Astra gate, but not dispatch under the target config directory, parity of refusal tokens, absence of a quota leg, transcript-derived canary telemetry, the unprobed-native disclosure in the successful-registration path, or separate conformance checks for result, completion, and progress in both Claude modes.
findings.suggestion: Add observable DoD cases for each omitted adapter invariant and both modes' result/completion/progress conformance behavior.
findings.evidence: The outcomes are promised at package/children/C14.md:3 and required by Spec B FR-S5 at specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1092–1113. DoD lines 6–9 do not cover them.

findings.title: C17 does not grade its dependency checks or full fail-closed behavior
findings.body: C17 promises checks for four declared dependencies and fail-closed behavior for authority-expanding acts. Its DoD checks no dependency and exercises only the missing-ladder case. It does not grade the absence behavior of the other non-default configuration items or confirm that defaults exist only for the five categories the spec permits.
findings.suggestion: Add one gradable check for each declared dependency and a table-driven absence/default test covering all thirteen configuration items and their stamped fail directions.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-E1 defines the four dependencies at specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1006–1020 and the complete fail direction at :1042–1050. C17 What promises both at package/children/C17.md:3, but DoD lines 6–9 test only profile mutation, stamped values, and missing ladder behavior.
